content: 1. Take one 45 mg tablet orally once daily. 2. If daily intake of calcium and/or vitamin D is insufficient, supplemental intake is recommended. 3. This medication has not been evaluated for use in patients with renal impairment and is therefore not recommended in such cases. 4. Use of this medication is contraindicated in patients with hepatic impairment. 5. The medication should be used for the shortest duration necessary to achieve treatment goals while considering the individual risks and benefits for each woman. 6. The tablet may be taken with or without food. 7. Swallow the tablet whole; do not chew, crush, or split it. 8. If a dose is missed, patients should take it as soon as they remember unless it is almost time for the next scheduled dose. In such cases, they should skip the missed dose and not take two doses at the same time. 9. The combination of ospemifene and bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens is contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic synergism, which increases the effects of both drugs. 10. Bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens decrease the effects of anastrozole, antithrombin alfa, antithrombin III, argatroban, bemiparin, bivalirudin, dalteparin, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, heparin, phenindione, and protamine by pharmacodynamic antagonism, and their use is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 11. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by increasing metabolism through hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Cimetidine, clarithromycin, erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate), itraconazole, ketoconazole, levoketoconazole, and nefazodone increase the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Rifabutin, rifampin, and St. John’s Wort decrease the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. A reduction in bazedoxifene exposure may increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. 15. Estrogens may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 16. Ambrisentan increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 17. Amikacin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 18. Amiodarone increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 19. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Amoxicillin, ampicillin, azithromycin, aztreonam, cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefamandole, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefepime/enmetazobactam, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, cephalexin, chloramphenicol, chlorhexidine oral, ciprofloxacin, clindamycin, and clarithromycin decrease the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 21. Clotrimazole decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 22. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
